title: Grill — multiple repositories in one card (#291)
summary:
Before this gets planned: **11 decisions** that change the shape of the build, plus **8 defaults** to confirm or override.

Start with the five in **Shape** — they decide the data model, the agent's working directory, what can be edited, and what the first release is. Every question carries a recommendation, so you can accept all non-one-way-door answers with one click and only touch what you disagree with.

Source: issue #291 (outside the repo — proposed to commit as `docs/specs/multi-repo-tasks.md`). Grounding: `docs/plans/multi-repo-tasks-investigation.md`.

proven.text: **Today a multi-repo payload is silently dropped.** `CreateTaskInput extends Partial<Task>`, so a `repositories` array is accepted by the HTTP body and ignored; a scratch probe returned `repositories = undefined` and materialized exactly one worktree.

evidence.label: the input type is a Partial<Task>, so unknown keys ride along
one worktree path per task, derived from the task id

proven.text: **A per-task workspace root is the only layout every harness can see.** Cursor and fx ACP advertise no `additionalDirectories` capability; fx also refused to read a file outside its session cwd. Claude, Codex, Gemini and Copilot expose `--add-dir` / include-directories, but that is not universal. Both ACP agents do accept a non-git directory as `session/new.cwd`.

evidence.label: harness capability matrix from live probes

proven.text: **`@` references already behave correctly under a workspace root.** `resolveAtPath` resolves `frontend/a.ts` inside the workspace and refuses `../outside/secret.ts`; the containment is a realpath check. That is why each repo worktree must live *under* the workspace, not beside it.

evidence.label: realpath containment

proven.text: **The worktree-id guard is deliberately one level deep.** `listWorktrees` treats every direct child of `<dataDir>/worktrees` as a task id, and `resolveWorktreeDir` refuses `/`, `\` and `..`. A nested `<task-id>/<repo>` layout needs a new strict two-level parser; relaxing this guard would widen an `rm -rf` surface.

evidence.label: the id guard

proven.text: **A naive change passes the current suite.** Adding a JSON column and a multi-select, without touching `prepareWorkdir`, `startTask`, the diff/status routes or `listWorktrees`, compiles and leaves every existing test green — while only the primary repo gets a worktree and the agent never sees the rest. The plan must add tests that assert two worktrees, a second repo in cwd, per-repo diff/PR and multi-repo teardown.

sections.title: Shape — the five that decide the build
sections.intro: These are the blocking ones. Their answers determine the data model, the on-disk layout, the agent's cwd and the acceptance bar.

questions.title: What does a multi-repo task look like to the agent?
questions.why: This decides the data model, the on-disk layout, the agent's cwd, whether every harness can see every repo, and how much diff/status/PR code changes.
questions.context: The issue asks for one card and **shared context** across repos. Your comment says worktrees must keep working. The evidence is that a workspace root containing one subdirectory per repo is the only layout every harness can see: Cursor/fx/OpenCode cannot add roots, and fx treats cwd as its workspace boundary. Keeping the primary repo as cwd would work only for Claude/Codex/Gemini/Copilot and would break `@` into the other repos.

evidence.label: the only cwd every spawn path uses today
P4/P6: Cursor and fx ACP have no extra-root capability; fx refuses outside-cwd reads

options.label: Per-task workspace root, one conversation
options.description: `<dataDir>/worktrees/<task-id>/` is the agent's cwd; each repo is a subdirectory with its own worktree and branch. One session sees all of them.
options.consequence: Works for all 8 harnesses; `@frontend/src` resolves inside cwd; single-repo tasks keep today's layout. Cost: cwd is not a git repo, so per-repo diff/status, `@` listing, Codex's git sandbox and project-config discovery all need work.
options.preview:
worktrees/
  <task-id>/            <- agent cwd (plain dir, not a repo)
    frontend/           <- git worktree, branch feature/auth
    backend/            <- git worktree, branch feature/auth
    infra/              <- git worktree, branch feature/auth

options.label: Primary repo cwd + extra directories
options.description: Keep today's primary worktree as cwd; create the others as siblings and pass them via `--add-dir` / include-directories / absolute paths.
options.consequence: Smaller change to diff/status, but Cursor, fx and OpenCode cannot see the extra repos, and `@` into them fails `resolveAtPath`. Would need per-harness gating or a degraded experience.
options.preview:
worktrees/
  <task-id>/        <- primary worktree, agent cwd
  <task-id>-backend/ <- sibling worktree, only visible with --add-dir

options.label: Coordinator + one agent per repo
options.description: One card, one lead conversation, one child agent/run per repo that reports back.
options.consequence: Contradicts the issue's single shared context; adds N sessions, branch coordination and PR attribution. Closer to a pipeline than a task.

recommendation.reason: It is the only layout that works for every harness without per-kind degradation, and it preserves the existing realpath containment for `@`.

questions.title: Which of the issue's six bullets ships in this change?
questions.why: It decides whether the plan needs per-repo diff/status, per-repo PR creation and their tests, or only the selection/worktree core.
questions.context: The six asks are: (1) select multiple repos on create/edit, (2) one worktree/branch per repo, (3) the agent can access and modify all of them, (4) shared context, (5) track progress/changes in one card, (6) review and create separate PRs per repo. A staged release that stops after (4) leaves the reporter's card unable to show or ship the other repos' changes.

evidence.label: one diff scope and one PR stamp today

options.label: All six bullets
options.description: Selection, per-repo worktrees, one agent seeing them, per-repo diff/status, and per-repo PR creation in one change.
options.consequence: Largest plan and the issue can be closed end-to-end. The per-repo PR UI is the extra surface; there is no bulk create-all flow in v1.

options.label: Core first (bullets 1–4), diff/PR second
options.description: Ship multiple selection, per-repo worktrees and shared agent context; leave per-repo diff/status and PR creation for a follow-up.
options.consequence: Faster first ship, but the card cannot show or land the other repos' changes — the reporter's actual workflow stays incomplete and the issue remains open.

options.label: Selection + worktrees only
options.description: Persist the repo list and materialize worktrees; the agent still runs in the primary repo.
options.consequence: Does not satisfy asks 3–6 and would be a misleading UI. Not recommended.

recommendation.reason: The issue's acceptance is the six bullets; shipping 1–4 still leaves the card unable to track or PR the extra repos.

questions.title: Must a multi-repo task use worktree isolation?
questions.why: Supporting `isolation: none` means the workspace must point at live checkouts, which either mutates the source repos or needs symlinks the current `resolveAtPath` containment rejects.
questions.context: `prepareWorkdir` returns `task.workdir` unchanged when isolation is none — there is no worktree to nest under a workspace root. Today `isolation: none` tasks are allowed to run directly in the project. The issue's own comment emphasizes worktrees, and the security model depends on agent-writable paths staying inside the task directory.

evidence.label: isolation none short-circuits before any worktree is created
the containment that makes `@` safe
evidence.code:
const withinCwd = realAbs === realCwd || realAbs.startsWith(realCwd + path.sep);
if (!withinCwd) return null;

options.label: Require worktree isolation for 2+ repos
options.description: Selecting a second repository forces/validates `isolation: "worktree"`; the mixed state is rejected at create with a clear error.
options.consequence: Each repo gets its own worktree and branch; no symlink or containment change; matches your comment. Single-repo tasks can still use `none`.
options.preview:
isolation: "worktree"  +  repositories: [frontend, backend, infra]  -> allowed
isolation: "none"      +  repositories: [frontend, backend]       -> 400

options.label: Support `none` via a symlinked/copied workspace
options.description: The workspace root contains links/copies to the live repos; the agent runs in it without worktrees.
options.consequence: Needs a new containment rule (realpath rejects links outside cwd), risks edits to the user's real checkouts, and adds a second teardown model. A much larger security surface.

options.label: Support `none` by running in the live repos
options.description: The workspace root exists only as a display path; the agent's real cwd is the first repo and the others are referenced absolutely.
options.consequence: No branch isolation at all; contradicts the worktree promise and reproduces the primary-cwd harness problem.

recommendation.reason: It keeps every agent-writable path inside the task directory and needs no relaxation of the realpath containment.

questions.title: When may the repository set change?
questions.why: Editing after worktrees exist means adding a repo with a branch created from that moment, and removing one means deciding what happens to its uncommitted work and commits.
questions.context: The issue explicitly asks to select repos when **creating or editing** a card. Today `workdir` is locked once a worktree exists (`PATCH /tasks/:id` returns 400), because the worktree is registered against the original repo. A pre-run edit is the safe middle: it satisfies 'editing a card' before any worktree exists, and it matches the existing lock.

evidence.label: the existing workdir lock

options.label: Editable until the first run creates worktrees
options.description: Add/remove/reorder repos while `worktreePath` is null; lock the set once materialized. Reordering can change the primary.
options.consequence: Satisfies 'editing' for drafts and pre-start cards; no worktree/commit preservation policy; matches today's workdir lock.

options.label: Fixed at creation
options.description: No edit UI for the repo set; change means a new task.
options.consequence: Simplest, but directly misses the issue's 'or editing a card' wording.

options.label: Editable after runs too
options.description: Add a repo mid-task (new worktree/branch from now) and remove one (decide keep/delete branch, dirty work, commits).
options.consequence: Most flexible, but needs a worktree/commit preservation policy, new teardown rules, and tests for add/remove during a live run. Large destructive surface.

recommendation.reason: It covers the issue's editing ask before any work exists and reuses the existing 'workdir is locked after a worktree' rule instead of inventing a preservation policy.

questions.title: What happens when one repo's worktree cannot be created at start?
questions.why: The failure mode decides whether the agent can ever run with a silent subset of the repos, and what the user sees when a source repo moved or a branch is already checked out.
questions.context: Preparing N worktrees is N git operations. A repo can be missing, not a git repo, have an unresolvable base ref, or already have the branch checked out elsewhere. Today a single failure returns `{ error }` before the agent spawns.

evidence.label: the single-repo failure contract
evidence.code: if ("error" in prepared) return { error: prepared.error };

options.label: All-or-nothing
options.description: Validate every repo, create all worktrees, and only then spawn. If one fails, remove the worktrees created in that attempt and return the failing repo's error.
options.consequence: The agent never runs with a missing repo; retries are idempotent because preparation reuses existing worktrees. Cost: cleanup logic for a mid-way failure.

options.label: Start with the repos that worked
options.description: Create what can be created, spawn the agent, and show the failed repo as an error chip on the card.
options.consequence: Faster to the first token, but a task silently missing its backend is worse than a failed start — especially for the issue's exact use case.

options.label: Stop and ask the user
options.description: Show a dialog listing failed repos with retry/skip; skip starts with the subset.
options.consequence: New UI state and no API/CLI equivalent; still allows a subset run.

recommendation.reason: A multi-repo task's premise is that all selected repos are present; a partial run is the failure the reporter would least expect.

questions.title: Which harnesses get multi-repo in the first release?
questions.why: It decides whether the plan carries a per-kind validation matrix and gating, or ships the workspace layout to every kind with smoke coverage where accounts exist.
questions.context: The workspace layout needs no extra-root capability, and both ACP agents accepted a non-git workspace as cwd. What is unproven is each kind's project-config discovery (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md in subdirectories) and Codex's git sandbox under a non-git cwd. Installed here: Claude, Codex, Cursor, fx. Not installed: Gemini, Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode.

evidence.label: Codex's git sandbox only sees the cwd's git common dir
P9: which installed CLIs expose extra-root flags

options.label: All eight, with a smoke matrix
options.description: Enable multi-repo for every kind under the workspace root. Live-smoke Claude/Codex/Cursor/fx; label Gemini/Copilot/Antigravity/OpenCode 'layout-supported, smoke pending' until accounts exist.
options.consequence: No gating and no second-class kinds; the risk is a per-kind config/sandbox surprise found during smoke. Fixes can land as follow-ups without changing the layout.

options.label: Only validated kinds
options.description: Hide/disable multi-repo unless the harness is on a validated allow-list (start with Claude and Codex).
options.consequence: Safest promise, but excludes Cursor/fx users — the exact kinds that cannot add roots and therefore need the workspace layout most.

options.label: All kinds, experimental badge
options.description: Enable everywhere but mark non-smoked kinds 'experimental' in the picker.
options.consequence: Honest, but adds a UI state and a support matrix to maintain; the badge has to be removed later by another change.

recommendation.reason: The layout is capability-free by design; gating would exclude the harnesses that motivated it, and the smoke matrix gives us evidence before claiming support.

questions.title: How do the repo directories reach the agent in the launch prompt?
questions.why: The prompt-text rule says Agetor adds no text of its own except a fixed list. A new 'Repositories:' block is a documented exception; reusing the references block is compliant.
questions.context: The agent will already see the repos as subdirectories of its cwd and can `ls`. But the launch prompt currently names the working directory and references; pipelines and CLI sends may need the repo list spelled out. The existing `formatReferences` helper already renders a heading plus one bullet per folder.

evidence.label: the existing block

options.label: Reuse the references block
options.description: Add each repo worktree directory as a folder reference. No new machine-added text or exception.
options.consequence: Compliant with the current rule and uses the same path the agent already reads. Less legible than a labeled repo list, and it mixes user attachments with task structure.

options.label: A new 'Repositories:' paragraph
options.description: A dedicated machine-added block naming each repo and its branch.
options.consequence: Clearest for the agent, but needs a documented exception to the prompt-text rule and an update to the rule's docs and tests.

options.label: No machine text
options.description: The workspace cwd is the only signal; the agent discovers the rest.
options.consequence: No rule change, but the agent may not know which subdirectories are task repos vs scratch files, and the issue's shared-context ask becomes implicit.

recommendation.reason: It keeps the documented prompt contract intact and reuses the helper both create-time and per-message paths already share.

questions.title: How are branch names and base refs chosen across repos?
questions.why: Each repo can have its own branch nomenclature and default branch; the answer decides the form layout and the branch uniqueness checks.
questions.context: `createTask` reads `projects.get(workdir)?.branchConfig` and renders a branch from a pattern, falling back to the legacy scheme. Repos commonly differ: `main` vs `master`, `feature/` vs `feat/`. A single shared base ref is wrong when the default branches differ.

evidence.label: branch naming already reads the project's config

options.label: Per-repo branch and base
options.description: Each repo derives its branch from its own `Project.branchConfig` and picks its own base ref; the form shows one compact row per repo.
options.consequence: Respects each repo's nomenclature and default branch; 3–5 rows of UI. Branch names may differ across repos, which is fine for separate PRs.

options.label: Same branch name everywhere, per-repo base
options.description: One branch name (from the primary's config or a task slug) applied to all repos; each repo keeps its own base ref.
options.consequence: Easy cross-repo correlation (`feature/auth` in all three) but ignores a repo whose config mandates another prefix; a repo may reject the name.

options.label: One branch and one base ref, overridable
options.description: A single branch/base pair applied to every repo, with per-repo overrides behind a disclosure.
options.consequence: Simplest UI, but a single base ref is wrong whenever the repos' default branches differ; the override path is the real complexity.

recommendation.reason: The branch settings already live on each project, and separate PRs make one shared branch name unnecessary.

questions.title: How do commit/push and PR creation work across repos?
questions.why: The existing `commitPushPrompt` and PR-proposal parser assume one branch; an aggregate flow needs multi-proposal parsing, while per-repo actions reuse today's machinery.
questions.context: The RunPanel has one 'Commit & push' chip and one 'Create PR' prefill driven by one `TaskGitStatus`. `POST /github/pull-create` stamps `tasks.pr_url` only when the task's workdir matches the PR's directory. The issue asks for separate PRs per repo, not one bulk action.

evidence.label: the single-branch prompt
the one-PR guard

options.label: Per-repo actions
options.description: Each repo row gets its own 'Commit & push' and 'Create PR'; the prompt names that repo's branch and the PR URL stamps that repo's entry.
options.consequence: Reuses the existing prompt, prefill and one-PR guard with a repo selector; safe and testable. Many clicks for 5 repos, and the PR-proposal parser keeps its one-proposal shape.

options.label: One aggregate flow
options.description: One 'Commit & push all' prompt lists every repo/branch and asks for one PR proposal per repo; one 'Create all PRs' action walks them.
options.consequence: Fewer clicks, but needs multi-proposal parsing, repo labels in the transcript, and a new aggregate prompt; more UI and parsing risk.

options.label: Aggregate commit, per-repo PR
options.description: One prompt commits/pushes every repo; PR creation stays a per-repo action with its own link.
options.consequence: Balances clicks and safety; still needs the multi-proposal parser for the commit prompt, but not a bulk PR action.

recommendation.reason: It is the smallest safe change to a contract that currently assumes one branch and one proposal, and it satisfies 'separate PRs' without new parsing.

questions.title: Do pipelines and issue-created tasks support multiple repos in v1?
questions.why: Pipelines share one parent worktree across step rows; the issue dialog reuses the project picker. Either the repo array propagates through them, or the feature must be hidden/rejected there.
questions.context: A pipeline parent prepares one worktree and copies `workdir`/`isolation`/`branch`/`worktreePath`/`baseRef` onto every step row; steps never materialize or own teardown. `CreateTaskFromIssueDialog` is rooted at the issue's repo. If multi-repo is offered in the shared New Task form but not these, users hit an inconsistent picker or a broken step.

evidence.label: step rows copy the parent's single worktree fields
evidence.code:
tasks.insert({
  id: childId,
  title: `${run.pipelineName} · ${step.name}`,
  prompt: composed,
  column: "ready",
  agent: profile.harness,
  workdir: parent.workdir,
  isolation: parent.isolation,
  taskType: parent.taskType,
  branch: parent.branch,
  branchSource: parent.branchSource,
  worktreePath: parent.worktreePath,
  checkoutBranch: parent.checkoutBranch ?? null,
  baseRef: parent.baseRef,

options.label: Both
options.description: Pipeline parents may be multi-repo (steps copy the workspace/repo array; teardown stays parent-owned). Create-from-issue can add extra repos, with the issue's repo as primary.
options.consequence: Consistent surfaces. Pipeline propagation and the issue PR body (`Closes #N` only on the issue's repo) need tests. Extra repos' PRs must not claim the issue.

options.label: Pipelines only
options.description: Pipeline parents support multiple repos; the issue dialog stays single-repo.
options.consequence: Covers the shared-worktree machinery but leaves the issue flow single; the picker divergence remains.

options.label: Issue tasks only
options.description: Create-from-issue can add repos; pipeline parents stay single.
options.consequence: Covers the reporter's GitHub-repo case but requires rejecting/hiding multi-repo in the pipeline form.

options.label: Neither — ordinary New Task only
options.description: Hide/reject multi-repo in both flows; a pipeline or issue task stays single-repo in v1.
options.consequence: Smallest v1, but a reviewer may call it unfinished because the shared picker appears in both flows, and the issue's exact use case is issue-driven work.

recommendation.reason: Pipelines already copy one parent worktree, so copying a repo array is the same rule; an issue task is exactly the cross-repo use case.

questions.title: How far does CLI/TUI parity go in this change?
questions.why: The API must accept repositories in every case; the question is whether `agetor add`, `show`, `shell`, `rm` and the TUI can create and display them in the same change.
questions.context: The house style keeps CLI/TUI in step with the webview (the at-file-references and harness-stacks docs both call out parity). The CLI is how scripts and agents create tasks, and its `--workdir` is single. The TUI create form is a separate, dense surface.

evidence.label: the single --workdir flag
one scope for the `@` popover

options.label: Full CLI + TUI parity
options.description: `agetor add --repo` (repeatable), `show`/`shell`/`rm` repo-aware, TUI multi-select and multi-scope `@` completion.
options.consequence: Matches house style and leaves no second-class surface; the TUI create form is the largest non-core piece and adds tests.

options.label: CLI create/read, TUI read-only
options.description: `add --repo` and `show`/`shell`/`rm` parity; the TUI displays multi-repo tasks and `@` scopes but its create form stays single-repo in v1.
options.consequence: Scripts and agents can create the feature; TUI users can inspect but not create. A smaller, honest gap documented as a follow-up.

options.label: Webview only
options.description: The API accepts repositories, but the CLI and TUI are unchanged.
options.consequence: Smallest change; `agetor add` cannot create the feature and `show`/`rm` show only the primary, which the house style treats as drift.

recommendation.reason: The CLI is the scriptable surface and must not be blind to the feature; the TUI create form can follow without blocking the issue.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Low-stakes defaults I'd bet on. Confirm each with one click, or override with what it should be. These are recorded as owner decisions; none is a one-way door.

questions.title: Primary-repo mirrors and backward compatibility
questions.why: Decides the shape old clients and the CLI read.

recommendation.value: `workdir`, `branch`, `worktreePath`, `baseRef`, `prUrl` stay the primary repo's mirrors; `repositories[]` is the source of truth. Legacy rows derive a one-entry array from the existing columns — no backfill. `existingBranch`, `issueUrl` and `isolation` stay primary/global. Document that an older build sees only the primary and may tear down only its worktree.
recommendation.reason: Additive, so old clients keep compiling; a downgrade guard would be a new migration for a case the user controls.

questions.title: Repo identity, primary selection and cap
questions.why: Prevents two worktrees of the same repo and bounds N-worktree cost.

recommendation.value: Dedupe by git root; the first selected repo is primary and can be reordered before the first run; hard cap 10 repositories per task (400 above that), with 2–5 the expected range.
recommendation.reason: Two registered projects under one git root would otherwise get two branches/worktrees; 10 bounds git and polling work without limiting real use.

questions.title: Workspace layout and Worktrees page
questions.why: This is the on-disk and API shape the plan builds against.

recommendation.value: Multi-repo workspace is `<dataDir>/worktrees/<task-id>/<slug>` (slug = repo basename, uniquified); single-repo tasks keep today's `<dataDir>/worktrees/<task-id>`. The Worktrees page shows one row per repo grouped under its task, with an opaque id `<taskId>__<slug>`; owned rows still route deletion to archiving the task, orphan rows keep per-row delete.
recommendation.reason: Nested paths stay inside the existing task-dir containment; the `__` id keeps one URL path segment and a strict two-level parser.

questions.title: Card, diff, filters and progress
questions.why: Decides what a user sees without opening a new page.

recommendation.value: New Task form shows one compact row per repo (branch/base) and collapses to today's form for one repo. Card shows the primary repo plus `+N`. Diff dialog gets per-repo tabs/selector. Repo filter and text search match any selected repo. Context menu gets a per-repo submenu. The agent's existing todo progress stays one shared list; per-repo change counts live in the run panel.
recommendation.reason: One card must show all repos without a new page; the todo list is conversation-scoped, not repo-scoped.

questions.title: Create-time validation
questions.why: Failing early is better than a half-created task.

recommendation.value: Create rejects with 400 if any selected repo is missing, is not a git repo, has an unresolvable base ref, has an invalid branch name, or has that branch checked out in another live task; nothing is created. `isolation: none` with 2+ repos is rejected with the worktree-required message.
recommendation.reason: Matches today's create-time base-ref and existing-branch validation and avoids discovering a bad repo at start.

questions.title: Archive and delete with dirty repos
questions.why: Protects uncommitted work without making a task unarchivable.

recommendation.value: Archive teardown is best-effort per repo: clean worktrees are detached, dirty ones are kept on disk with their branch, and every per-repo outcome is reported. Archive still succeeds. Delete is explicit and per repo; it never deletes a `branchSource: existing` branch.
recommendation.reason: It is exactly what `detachWorktree` does today; all-or-nothing would make one dirty repo block archiving the card.

questions.title: Terminals, polling and extra roots
questions.why: These are the 5 s-poll and multi-process constraints the plan must not violate.

recommendation.value: Terminals open at the workspace root (with a repo selector); `/tasks/:id/git-status` returns all repo statuses in one batched response per poll; each repo is also passed as an extra root (`--add-dir` / include-directories) where the harness supports it, even though cwd is the workspace.
recommendation.reason: 5 s × N repos would exceed the webview connection budget; extra roots help project-config discovery and Codex's git sandbox.

questions.title: Spec and acceptance
questions.why: The contract is outside the repo today; the plan must cite a path a reviewer can open.

recommendation.value: Commit the issue's asks and these decisions as `docs/specs/multi-repo-tasks.md` before planning. Add one e2e spec covering create → fake-driver run → two worktrees/branches → per-repo diff → per-repo PR stamp → archive teardown, plus unit tests for per-repo prepare/reuse/cleanup, nested worktree ids and route policy, and pipeline step copy.
recommendation.reason: The issue is a tracker tab, and the current suite passes a naive multi-select that creates one worktree.
